description: Eight advocacy briefs by ADEB LONODJI for Bédjondo, Chad: broadband, electricity, drinking water, health, roads, education, vocational training, and a note to the commune.
title: Eight briefs for Bédjondo
lede: Broadband, electricity, drinking water, health, roads and bridges, education, vocational training, and a note to the commune: what we ask of the State, regulators, operators and partners, and what we commit to in return.

sections.html:
Eight briefs

What we ask, of whom, and what we commit to

Each brief sets out a sourced diagnosis, what the change would make possible, precise requests to named recipients, and the association’s own commitments. All are published in French, sent officially, and tracked publicly (sending date, replies, results). English summaries below.

Broadband internetPublished

Broadband internet

Bédjondo is a broadband white zone with the most expensive small data bundles. We ask for priority in the 200 new 3G/4G sites and universal service, published coverage maps, rural tariffs and an accessible Starlink outlet. We commit to co-fund a community digital space and to run a citizen speed-measurement campaign.

Recipients
Ministry of Telecommunications, ARCEP (regulator), Airtel, Moov Africa, Salam, Starlink Chad

ElectricityPublished

Electricity

Chad has 6 % electricity access (1–2 % rural). We ask that Bédjondo and its cantons be included in the PAAET and Mission 300, public facilities first, with subsidised solar kits. We commit to solar street lighting for the market with the diaspora, and to a needs survey.

Recipients
Ministry of Energy, SNE, CEP-TchadElec (PAAET), ARSE, World Bank / Mission 300, mini-grid operators
Read (FR)PDF (FR)
Drinking waterPublished

Drinking water

A departmental capital without a water network. We ask for an inventory of water points, a solar mini-network (borehole, water tower, standpipes), water and latrines in every school and at the health centre, and management committees. We commit to the inventory and to emergency repairs.

Recipients
Ministry of Water, PAEPA SU MR (AfDB), UNICEF, Caritas Switzerland / NexSud, commune

HealthPublished

Health

One woman in a hundred dies in childbirth in Chad. We ask for a midwife and a nurse, a basic laboratory, a solar cold chain, an obstetric emergency kit, an ambulance and a referral protocol to Koumra, and a health mutual. We commit to solar equipment for the maternity ward and medical missions from the diaspora.

Recipients
Ministry of Public Health, provincial health delegation, Koumra provincial hospital, partners
Read (FR)PDF (FR)
Roads and bridgesPublished

Roads and bridges

The Koumra–Bédjondo road is cut in the rainy season; women have asked since 2023 for a bridge on the Bédjondo–Békamba road; the Hoblo bridge is broken. We ask for an all-season road, both bridges, and local maintenance crews. We commit to a documented survey of roads and breaking points.

Recipients
Ministry of Infrastructure, PMCR rural mobility project (World Bank), road maintenance fund, commune
Read (FR)PDF (FR)
EducationPublished

Education

73 pupils per teacher, classes of 83, community teachers paid late, a secondary school without a laboratory. We ask for qualified teachers, solid classrooms with water and latrines, an equipped lycée, continuity of the ProQEB programme, canteens and vocational training. We commit to a solar-powered exam room, mentoring and scholarships.

Recipients
Ministry of Education, provincial delegation, ProQEB / Swiss cooperation, UNICEF, commune
Read (FR)PDF (FR)
Vocational trainingPublished

Vocational training

Bédjondo’s vocational training centre is listed in the national register but has never opened. We ask for it to open on nine trades that the area actually needs — carpentry, metalwork and welding, solar, borehole drilling, masonry, agro-processing, tailoring, mechanics and digital skills — with apprenticeships funded by FONAP and examinations held on site. We commit to surveying local demand and to mobilising trainers from the diaspora.

Recipients
Ministry responsible for vocational training, FONAP, provincial delegation, commune
Read (FR)PDF (FR)
Note to the communePublished

Note to the commune

Six proposals for a commune equal to its town: a public and enforceable development plan, transparent own revenues, partnership agreements, an open council, a first visible project (solar lighting of the market), and free studies from the diaspora.

Recipients
Mayor and council of Bédjondo, prefect of Mandoul Occidental

Public follow-up, support form, citizen speed measurements and the participatory needs map are on the French pages: Nos plaidoyers · Carte des besoins. Partners who wish to respond or to support a brief can write to us in English.
